summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs customer's current baseline provider. Redwood outperformed baseline on p95 latency and throughput after quantization and batching tweaks. Discussion covered warm vs cold starts, KV/prefix caching, networking (VPC) overhead, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: share detailed bench spreadsheet, config artifacts, customer to provide production traffic sample, schedule VPC deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see the core team here. Were going to walk through the latest benchmark runs comparing Redwood runs to the baseline provider you have in prod. Aim is to surface wins and any tuning left.
[00:17] Jordan (Nextera CTO): Thanks Alex, on time. Weve got Samir, Tanya and Marta on. Appreciate the update.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood SE): quick note, some of the model names in the sheet got auto-corrected by the export so ignore weird spellings, like "Redwood-2" coming out as "Red-wood two" in one column, sorry about that.
[00:40] Samir (ML Eng): no worries, Priya. We mostly care latency p95, throughput, and any quality diffs after quantization. The baseline provider is what we use in prod currently so baseline numbers are in the sheet.
[00:52] Alex: right, ok so high level first: after applying the q4_8 quantization profile, enabling prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and a small batching change (max batch 8, dynamic batching window 20ms), we saw consistent p95 improvements and throughput gains versus baseline.
[01:10] Priya: to call out numbers from the sheet quick: for the 512-token convo workload the baseline provider p95 was ~580ms, Redwood running hosted with our q4_8 profile was ~320ms p95. Median latencies were 120ms baseline vs 70ms Redwood. Throughput (sustained RPS with 95% token completeness) baseline ~5 rps, Redwood ~8 rps. Cost per 1k tokens estimated: baseline $0.80, Redwood $0.50 (these are run-time estimates with caching & batching).
[01:35] Tanya (SRE): Those are promising. A couple clarifying qns: were those runs cold starts or warmed VMs? Network overhead? We care about VPC egress latency.
[01:45] Priya: Great question. The numbers I just quoted are warm runs — we did a cold-start sweep too. Cold-start p95 for the first request hits roughly ~1.1s on Redwood hosted (cold VM + model load), baseline was ~1.8s. For production we recommend a small warm pool or pre-warming for low-latency lanes — thats configurable in Dedicated.
[02:05] Jordan: What about Private / VPC, our compliance team will require VPC with customer-managed egress. Does VPC add a big latency tax?
[02:12] Priya: For our VPC option we measured an average overhead of 10-30ms depending on egress path and SNAT behavior, in worst cases 60ms. The sheet has the VPC run column labeled "vpc-nat-01". The major variable is how the cloud provider routes egress—sometimes we see additional hop. We can do a run inside your VPC for exact numbers.
[02:30] Samir: Good. On the quality/front, are we seeing any regression post-quant? We care about the hallucination rate and some token-level diffs.
[02:38] Priya: We ran the evaluation set you shared (the 300 prompt eval) — quality delta was negligible for typical completion tasks. We did see minor probability shifts for very rare token outputs; those are flagged in the "eval_regressions" tab. If you have strict pass/fail thresholds we can run additional scans or use a mixed-precision profile.
[02:58] Marta (Product): Is there any scenario where Redwood would underperform baseline for our workload?
[03:04] Priya: Yes — for extremely long sequence lengths ( > 4k tokens ) and very small batch sizes of 1 without KV cache, the baseline optimized kernel in their backend had an advantage on sustained throughput in our tests. But for your 512-1024 typical sequences and chat style workload, Redwood is better after tuning.
[03:20] Alex: Also note the baseline provider has higher variance in p95 — their 99th percentile spikes more often during bursts. We saw more graceful degradation during simulated traffic spikes with our fallback routing.
[03:33] Jordan: How much of the perf gain is from quantization vs your runtime/batching? I need to explain this to procurement.
[03:40] Priya: breakdown is in the spreadsheet ("delta breakdown" sheet) but high-level: about 45% of the p95 improvement came from optimized kernels and serving runtime (our continuous batching + kv cache), 35% from q4_8 quant gains, and 20% from network/instance selection (we used A100-like topology). The cost reduction is mostly caching + quantization.
[04:00] Samir: Can you share the exact run command and the docker/container config? We want to reproduce locally for one microbenchmark.
[04:07] Priya: absolutely, Ill share run-commands and configs — those are in the artifacts link I'll post after the call. It's a small shell script and a tfserving-style config.
[04:15] Tanya: Are there any license or model residency concerns with the q4 profiles? Legal asked about redistributing quantized model weights.
[04:23] Alex: We ship Redwood-verified model variants under our model catalog; licensing depends on the upstream model license. For open models it's generally permitted to quantize for inference but we can put whatever we ship in your private repo. If you need air-gapped on-prem we have a private deployment option. We'll loop in legal for the exact license language.
[04:41] Jordan: On procurement, rough timeline: if we like final numbers we have a procurement window in the next 2-3 weeks. Any blockers on your side for a Dedicated contract?
[04:51] Alex: Contracting is straightforward—our sales ops can give a term sheet. The main engineering work is final production validation and the VPC network run we discussed. We'll support a short pilot extension if you need more runs.
[05:01] Marta: About regression alerts, does Redwood instrument quality monitoring against the prompt set? We need automated alerts if eval metrics cross thresholds after a rollout.
[05:09] Priya: Yes our Redwood Console offers quality/regression monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals. We can configure alerting to send to your Slack or webhook and tie it into rollouts (canary abort on regressions).
[05:20] Samir: Back to the bench numbers — can you repeat the most relevant table values for the 512-token chat typical route? I want to take notes.
[05:26] Priya: Sure. Baseline provider (prod) p95: ~580ms; median ~120ms; throughput ~5 rps. Redwood hosted (q4_8 + kv+batch8) p95: ~320ms; median ~70ms; throughput ~8 rps. Cost per 1k tokens (estimated observed): baseline $0.80; Redwood $0.50. Cold-start p95: baseline ~1.8s vs Redwood ~1.1s. VPC overhead: +10-60ms depending on path.
[05:50] Jordan: That's helpful. Any outlier runs?
[05:53] Priya: We had two outlier runs during baseline testing with CPU throttling on their side; we filtered them in the "cleaned" tab. Also note our runs with batch windows above 30ms raise median but improve throughput; we tuned for median p95 balance.
[06:05] Alex: We should talk about burst handling: Redwood has a fallback model variant and multi-region routing that keeps tail latency bounded. We can simulate your production bursts and show results.
[06:16] Tanya: Please do. Also we will want to see audit logs and KMS integration for Private.
[06:21] Alex: Yep SOC2 and KMS integration lines are in our security packet, I'll share that link.
[06:26] [07:00] Speaker 5: -- (inaudible)
[07:03] Priya: Quick note on tuning knobs we changed: 1) max_batch_size 8, 2) dynamic_window 20ms, 3) kv_cache enabled for repeated session tokens, 4) q4_8 quant profile with fallback bitcast. Those are in the config well post.
[07:20] Samir: For our internal perf tests well want the exact docker image SHA.
[07:24] Priya: will include image SHAs in the artifacts.
[07:27] Jordan: On cost math, does the $0.50 include infra amortization for Dedicated?
[07:32] Alex: The $0.50 is an observed run-time cost for hosted with caching and quant. For Dedicated pricing we'd model committed capacity differently — unit cost can be lower at scale but theres a reservation. We can produce a cost model against your traffic sample.
[07:45] Marta: Any concerns about tokenization differences vs baseline? We use a slightly different tokenizer in preproc sometimes.
[07:51] Priya: Tokenization differences can cause small token-count deltas — we normalize inputs in the bench harness and included raw token counts in the sheet. If you want we can run with your exact preproc.
[07:59] Alex: OK next steps recap: Alex will send annotated spreadsheet and security packet; Priya will post run commands, quant configs, and docker SHAs; Samir to drop traffic sample and confirm data residency; we'll schedule the VPC deep dive. Anything else?
[08:14] Jordan: That sounds good. Also can you add a column for p99 in the next sheet export? procurement asked for p99.
[08:20] Priya: yep will add p99 and cold-start distributions.
[08:24] Alex: Great. Thanks all for the time. Well follow up with artifacts and timeline.
[08:29] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Bye.
[08:32] (call ends)
